advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the ADR slug-placement rationale with actual gen_adr_index.py classification (bare 'config' is not a 'Config & CLI' key; the entry lands in 'Other decisions').
evidence: scripts/gen_adr_index.py lines 170-185: the 'Config & CLI' group keys are ('config-write','onboard','editing-prompt-contracts','aliases','module-size','unified-criteria-registry','mcp-optional-auth','calibration','exit-11','workflow-as-gate','execution-mode') — no bare 'config'
scripts/gen_adr_index.py line 207: `if any(k in slug for k in keys)` — substring match; slug 'operation-scoped-config-and-provider-composition' does not contain 'config-write'
README diff appends the entry under the section ending at 'Other decisions' (README.md line 127 header, entry at line 135), consistent with FALLBACK, NOT 'Config & CLI'
Ticket 23e9-cad1-64bf-4bb7 description: 'The slug deliberately avoids the generic word `bindings`... this keeps the application-wide decision in the Config & CLI index section.'
advisory.finding: The ADR ticket's stated slug-classification rationale is inconsistent with the actual generator behavior: it claims the slug keeps the entry in the 'Config & CLI' index section because the generator classifies on the word 'config', but gen_adr_index.py's 'Config & CLI' keyword list contains 'config-write' (not bare 'config'), so the slug 'operation-scoped-config-and-provider-composition' matches no group and falls to the 'Other decisions' fallback — which is where the README diff correctly places it. The generated artifact is correct, but the intent/rationale is wrong about how classification works.
